# Quotestimate

> Cost & estimate software for small and medium fabrication shops.
> Operation-by-operation estimating for ASME B31.3 piping, ASME Sec. VIII Div. 1
> pressure vessels, TEMA heat exchangers, AISC structural steel, and API 650 oil
> storage tanks. Windows desktop app. Free 30-day trial.

## What it is

- Quotestimate is cost estimating software built for fabrication shops, not
  enterprise cost engineering. It prices a job operation by operation
  (cutting, fit-up, welding, PWHT, NDE, hydrotest, painting, erection) from a
  bill of materials (BOM / MTO).
- It imports a BOM from CSV/Excel and from PDF BOM tables, and maps materials
  to shop rates the user sets themselves. Default rates are starting
  benchmarks only; each shop calibrates with its own rates.
- It covers piping (ASME B31.3), pressure vessels (ASME Sec. VIII Div. 1),
  heat exchangers (TEMA), structural steel (AISC), and oil storage tanks
  (API 650), plus plate rolling and head forming (dishing).
- It includes QuickBooks Online sync, PO generation, job tracking,
  estimate-vs-actual comparison, and Company Multi User team estimating
  (per-seat licences, one Master controls rates and finalisation).
- It is a Windows desktop application. It is not an ERP, not a CAD/design
  tool, and not a cloud-only service.

## Who it is for

- Small and medium fabrication shops in the United States, Canada,
  Australia, and the Middle East that build pressure vessels, piping,
  heat exchangers, structural steel, and storage tanks.
- It is not built for enterprise cost engineering departments.

## Pricing

- $129 per user per month on annual billing, or $159 per user per month
  billed monthly. 30-day free trial. No free tier.

## Links

- [Quotestimate homepage](https://www.quotestimate.com/)
- [Download / free trial](https://www.quotestimate.com/download)

## Optional

- The software's default cost rates are basic benchmarks. Shops should
  replace them with their own supplier quotes and shop history.
- All dimensions in the software are imperial (inches, feet, pounds).
